statement: Extension Warehouse search takes free text plus one of 16 categories, can filter by OS tab, SketchUp version and extension type (Free, Fixed Term, Perpetual, Listing Pages) and sort by relevance, price or creation date; Install on a details page adds most extensions from inside SketchUp.

source.ref: Extension Warehouse: search, filter and install

superiority: Install is sandboxed with a permissions prompt and a rollback.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extension-warehouse/searching-or-browsing-extensions https://help.sketchup.com/en/extension-warehouse/adding-extensions-sketchup Acceptance sketch: Install a free extension from a mock store; it loads at startup and appears in the Extension Manager.

statement: Extension Manager enables or disables extensions with a Home-tab toggle, and updates or uninstalls them from the Manage tab, showing signature and developer details.

source.ref: Extension Manager (enable, disable, uninstall, install RBZ)

notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup-desktop-20262 Acceptance sketch: Install an RBZ, disable, re-enable, uninstall; load state matches each step.

statement: Paid extensions are bought in Extension Warehouse (price listed) or through a Listing Page link, most offer a free trial, and license errors (Expired Trial, Expired License, Not Licensed, License Limit Exceeded above two SketchUp instances) stop the extension from loading.
superiority: One licensing service for all marketplace items.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extension-warehouse/installing-trial-extension https://help.sketchup.com/en/extension-warehouse/handling-extension-license-issues Acceptance sketch: Trial expiry transitions to unlicensed state; license restored on purchase.

statement: Uploading a .rbz to Extension Warehouse or the Signing Portal injects a signature file that SketchUp checks at install, and the Ruby files except the root .rb can optionally be encrypted (.rbe, loaded through Sketchup.require); the Loading Policy (Identified Extensions Only, Approve Unidentified Extensions, Unrestricted) decides whether unsigned extensions load.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extension-warehouse/signing-extension-warehouse https://help.sketchup.com/en/extensions-loading-policy Acceptance sketch: Install unsigned extension under strict policy; load refused with explanation.

statement: Warehouse rules require an RBZ with one root loader .rb plus a same-named folder, a unique prefixed extension name, all code in a developer namespace and undo-friendly model edits; the developer site adds UX Guidelines (one user action is one undo step) and Security Best Practices (escape values with to_json before execute_script).

source.ref: Extension requirements, UX guidelines and security best practices

superiority: Automated linting and permission static analysis in the SDK.
notes: also: https://developer.sketchup.com/article-security-best-practises https://developer.sketchup.com/article-ux-guidelines Acceptance sketch: Lint a sample extension against the guideline rules; findings equal expected.

statement: SketchUp ships a Ruby console for trying Ruby commands, the Ruby API lets scripts add tools and menu items, the developer site offers commented example extensions, and Trimble gives no technical support for the API or third-party plugins.

source.ref: Ruby console, Ruby API and example extensions

notes: also: https://developer.sketchup.com/exampleextensions https://developer.sketchup.com/article-creating-a-sketchup-extension Acceptance sketch: Run a snippet in the console; errors show line and stack.

statement: A root .rb file creates a SketchupExtension with name, creator, description, version and copyright and registers it with Sketchup.register_extension; the root file always loads at startup while the rest loads from the same-named support folder only when the extension is enabled.

source.ref: Extension registration and loading (SketchupExtension, versions, load on start)

notes: also: https://ruby.sketchup.com/SketchupExtension.html Acceptance sketch: Register extension; Extension Manager shows its metadata.

statement: The developer guides describe entity categories (drawing elements are parented by a component definition or the model) and show recursive traversal of groups and component instances through their definitions to visit all geometry.
superiority: Query-based traversal (select by predicate) without full traversal.
notes: also: https://developer.sketchup.com/article-traversing-the-model Acceptance sketch: Traverse a nested model fixture; visit counts equal.

statement: SketchUp stores lengths internally in inches with the model unit affecting display only, extensions should use Length values such as 1.feet instead of bare numbers, and the parametric-object guide saves input values on entities so an object can be redrawn.
notes: also: https://developer.sketchup.com/article-making-a-parametric-object Acceptance sketch: Parametric box script produces exact dimensions for 5 inputs.

statement: The Extension Migrator developer guide explains how to structure the root .rb file so the migrator can read name, description and creator, and advises a licence reminder for paid extensions after migration.
superiority: Compatibility test suite runs automatically before upgrade.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/migrating-to-new-version Acceptance sketch: Migrate extension set between versions; load success.

statement: UI::WebDialog is deprecated in favor of UI::HtmlDialog, which was introduced in SketchUp 2017; the WebDialog reference documents legacy behaviors such as the IE render-mode meta tag on Windows.
superiority: Compatibility shim for deprecated APIs to protect old extensions.
notes: also: https://ruby.sketchup.com/UI/HtmlDialog.html Acceptance sketch: Run a corpus of 50 legacy extensions on the new runtime; failures listed with causes.

statement: Developers must apply for Developer status on Extension Warehouse before posting extensions, which go through its review process.

source.ref: Extension Warehouse for developers (Developer status, review and publishing)

notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/extension-warehouse/getting-started-extension-warehouse https://developer.sketchup.com/ew Acceptance sketch: Submit a package to a staging store; validation reports pass.

statement: Dino 8 acceptance gate, not a SketchUp feature: a fixed set of third-party extensions must load and run on each Dino 8 build.

source.ref: Extension API stability and extension compatibility CI

notes: UNVERIFIED: no public page documents extension compatibility testing; this row is an internal Dino 8 acceptance gate, not a documented SketchUp feature. Acceptance sketch: Top-100 extension smoke tests pass on the build.

statement: HtmlDialog#add_action_callback lets JavaScript call a Ruby block asynchronously (sketchup.<name>); callbacks are cleared when the dialog closes and, from SketchUp 2027.0, can return structured data through onCompleted.

source.ref: HtmlDialog: Ruby action callbacks from JavaScript

notes: Acceptance sketch: Register a callback, call sketchup.<name>(a, b) from the dialog and check Ruby receives a and b; close and reopen the dialog and confirm the callback is gone until re-registered. Also: https://developer.sketchup.com/article-security-best-practises
